meta.title: A parser for DEC's ANSI-compatible video terminals
meta.author: Paul Flo Williams
meta.extraction_method: Parsed from the page's inline SVG state diagram (semantic element ids: state-*, legend-<src>-to-<dst>) plus the State/Action Definitions prose; cross-checked against haberman/vtparse tables.
meta.scope: Terminal-side parser (host-to-terminal byte stream) for DEC's 8-bit ANSI-compatible terminals, VT220 through VT525. Single-byte character encodings only; no UTF-8.

semantics.events: Events are raw input bytes, written in hex. Comma-separated sets; N-M is an inclusive range.
semantics.internal_events: An event listed under a state's 'on' happens without leaving the state; no entry/exit actions fire.
transition_order: exit action of the old state (if any)
entry action of the new state (if any)
semantics.anywhere_rule: Transitions listed under 'anywhere' apply from every state and take precedence over the state's own rules. The diagram never overlaps them with state-local rules.
semantics.self_transition: An anywhere transition that lands on the current state still fires its exit action and then its entry action (e.g. 1B received while in escape re-runs clear).
semantics.gr_gl_rule: Bytes A0-FF (GR) are treated identically to bytes 20-7F (GL): resolve A0-FF by looking up (byte - 0x80), but hand the ORIGINAL byte to the action. This symmetry does NOT extend to the C0 (00-1F) and C1 (80-9F) areas. Source: X3.64 Appendix H, restated on the diagram.

actions.ignore: The byte has no effect; drop it.
actions.print: Ground only. Map the byte to a glyph via current character-set mappings and shift states, and display it. 20 (SP) and 7F (DEL) print or are ignored depending on whether a 94- or 96-character set is mapped in.
actions.execute: Execute the C0 or C1 control function of this byte immediately. No parameters.
actions.clear: Forget the current private marker, intermediate characters, final character and parameters. Entry action of escape, csi_entry and dcs_entry.
actions.collect: Store the private marker (3C-3F) or intermediate character (20-2F) for the eventual dispatch. If more than two intermediates arrive, set an overflow flag so the dispatch becomes a no-op.
actions.param: Accumulate a parameter string: digits 30-39 append to the current parameter, 3B starts the next one. At most 16 parameters are stored; extras are silently discarded. Values must range at least to 16383; larger values clamp. Empty or 0 both mean 'use the control function's default'.
actions.esc_dispatch: Final byte of an escape sequence arrived: choose the control function from collected intermediates plus this final byte, and execute it.
actions.csi_dispatch: Final byte of a control sequence arrived: choose the control function from private marker, intermediates and this final byte, and execute it with the parameter list.
actions.hook: Final byte of the first part of a device control string arrived: choose the DCS function from private marker, intermediates and final, execute it, and select a handler to receive the data string that follows.
actions.put: Pass this data-string byte to the handler selected by hook. C0 controls are passed too.
actions.unhook: The device control string ended (via ST, CAN, SUB or ESC): tell the handler 'end of data' so it can finish cleanly. Exit action of dcs_passthrough.
actions.osc_start: OSC recognised: initialise the OSC string handler. Entry action of osc_string.
actions.osc_put: Pass this byte of the OSC string to the OSC handler as it arrives.
actions.osc_end: The OSC string ended (via ST, CAN, SUB or ESC): let the OSC handler finish cleanly. Exit action of osc_string.

notes: dcs_passthrough, dcs_ignore, osc_string and sos_pm_apc_string have no state-local exit transitions: they are left only via the anywhere rules (ST 9C, its 7-bit form ESC \ via 1B, CAN 18, SUB 1A, or any C1). That is why unhook and osc_end are exit actions.

ESC cancels any sequence in progress. A control string terminated by 7-bit ST (1B 5C) actually ends at the 1B (exit action fires there); the following 5C dispatches the ST control function, which is a no-op.

C0 controls are EXECUTED immediately inside escape sequences and control sequences (interleaving is legal: CSI 2 LF C moves the cursor right twice and down once), but are IGNORED in the first part of a device control string (dcs_entry/dcs_param/dcs_intermediate) and inside OSC strings. In the DCS data string they are passed through via put.

CAN and SUB cancel the sequence in progress; SUB additionally displays the error character (reversed question mark). This is VT220/VT420/VT500 behaviour; the VT320 documented CAN/SUB as no longer cancelling.
On terminals before the VT500, NUL (00) was discarded before parsing as a time-fill character. The VT500 processes NUL like any other C0 because of DECNULM (Null Mode).
3A (colon) anywhere in a CSI parameter string makes the whole sequence ignored (collected but never dispatched); it has no standardised meaning in X3.64 / on DEC terminals.
Private markers 3C-3F are only valid as the first byte after CSI/DCS; DEC used only 3D, 3E, 3F. A private marker later in the parameter string sends the sequence to the ignore state.

Parameter limits (VT500): unlimited parameter-string length, at most 16 parameters kept, values supported at least to 16383 (clamp above). Later parameters override earlier ones on conflict (CSI 7;0 m ends up with attributes off).

Parameter defaults: an empty parameter and the value 0 both select the control function's default (which is often 1, sometimes 100, sometimes absent — 0 is NOT 'the default value' itself). ECMA-48 distinguishes empty from 0, so implementations should keep them distinct internally.

In ground, 20 (SP) and 7F (DEL) depend on the mapped character set: 94-set GL prints space for 20 and ignores 7F; 96-set GL may print both. VT220-only emulation may always ignore 7F; VT320+ (ISO Latin-1) must be able to print it.
OSC strings only ever invoked DECSIN (Set Icon Name) and DECSWT (Set Window Title) on the VT520/VT525; earlier terminals ignored OSC content like PM/APC.
The VT420/VT500 can SEND APC strings (key press reports) to the host, but no DEC terminal assigns meaning to RECEIVED SOS/PM/APC strings; they are consumed and discarded.
